task: Implement the smallest reviewed V3 application checkpoint release/deployment foundation needed so future green Svelte checkpoints can be deployed to Contabo for owner testing. Work ONLY in repository code/config/tests/docs on release/v3-checkpoint-deploy; do NOT connect to production, deploy, restart services, read production secrets, access the production database, run migrations, change DNS, or mutate any live environment. Authority: docs/development/v3-application-stack-decision.md. Current read-only evidence: production host identity is ed-finder-prod / nb79a3d.mevnode.com; V3 currently runs stale edfinder-v3-api:phase4c-r5 plus edfinder-v3-proxy, edfinder-v3-public-auth-edge, PostgreSQL 18, Redis and NATS; public health is currently 503; no built frontend bundle exists; the authorized ed-new operator workflow currently has no deploy operation. Build a release mechanism that follows the locked rules: no git pull/build/dependency resolution on production; immutable OCI web/backend images tied to one exact Git SHA; static SvelteKit output served by nginx; same-origin routing keeps /api/*, exact /openapi.json and numeric /s/{id64} backend-owned and leaves application routes to Svelte; a machine-readable release manifest records exact Git SHA, image digests, migration/schema identity or checksum evidence, schema-compatibility status and rollback eligibility; production secrets remain external/mounted and never enter images/logs/manifests/source; deployment may recreate ONLY explicitly named V3 application services and must preserve the PostgreSQL 18 data service. Prefer a dedicated GitHub Actions release workflow that builds/pushes immutable images from an explicitly selected commit and a separate environment-gated deploy job/allowlisted operator action that consumes only the verified manifest/digests. The deploy path must fail closed on wrong host identity, mutable/non-digest images, missing manifest fields, unknown schema compatibility, missing secrets/config authority, unexpected service/container targets, or inability to identify an eligible rollback manifest. Application-only rollback must fail closed if compatibility with the current DB migration set is absent/unknown. Reuse the existing ED_NEW_OPERATOR_* SSH/known-host trust boundary rather than creating new secrets. Add structural/unit tests proving these safety properties and proving that normal PR/merge events do NOT auto-deploy. Document an owner-friendly checkpoint cadence: exact-head green -> merge to main -> build immutable release -> explicit deploy -> health/OpenAPI/session/Svelte route smoke -> receipt -> owner live test; rollback is explicit and receipt-backed. Do not implement database rollback/recovery or migrations. Do not modify the Svelte migration branches. If current repository/runtime evidence is insufficient to safely define an executable host deployment step, implement the build+manifest path and a deliberately fail-closed deploy preflight that reports exactly which topology/secret-mount facts remain required, rather than guessing. Run focused tests, workflow/YAML validation, image/Dockerfile checks practical without production, and git diff --check. Push the result to release/v3-checkpoint-deploy with exact-head lease and report precisely what is executable now versus still fail-closed.
